newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March spot natgas prices recover slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March spot natgas prices recover slightly.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for March 1 delivery recovered slightly Wednesday from yesterday's lows, but most prices remained more than a $1 per mmBtu under February indices, sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices for March edged about two to three cents higher to the mid-$1.70s, still sharply lower than February indices in the $2.80s.
Henry Hub gas sold mostly in the low-$1.80s, though some late morning deals were reported done in the high-$1.70s.
February prices for Thursday delivery also rose by about two to three cents to the mid-$1.80s.
In south Texas, March prices moved into the low-to-mid $1.60s, still more than a $1 under February indices.
Houston Lighting and Power's 1,250 megawatt South Texas 2 nuclear unit was operating at 29 percent of capacity early this morning and increasing power.
In the Permian basin, March gas prices remained in the $1.54-1.60 range, while San Juan values were also steady around $1.48-1.49.
Permian prices for Thursday delivery regained about five cents to the low-to-mid $1.80s as a brief cold front swept across western Texas.
Southern California border prices for March jumped into the mid-$1.60s, up at least 10 cents from Tuesday's levels but still a $1 under February indices.
Helping to keep a lid on prices was news that Bonneville Power Administration was again offering 200 megawatts (MW) of power for Thursday delivery.
In the Midcontinent, March prices climbed about three cents higher to the mid-$1.60s, still holding about a $1.10 discount to February 1 levels.
Chicago city-gate gas for next month sold in the high-$1.80s to low-$1.90s, sources said.
February prices in the Midcontinent were also a bit higher around $1.75 on most of the pipes.
In the East, New York city-gate prices for March 1 also edged up about two cents to the $2.10-2.15 area, down about $1.50 from February indices.
